subdomains.business_boundary: Professional modeling, engineering, and management of water quantity and quality across surface water, groundwater, and water infrastructure systems - spanning watershed hydrology, flood risk, stormwater/drainage design, and drinking-water distribution.
subdomains.occupations: civil/water-resources engineer; hydrologist; hydrogeologist/groundwater modeler; stormwater/drainage engineer; floodplain manager; water utility engineer
subdomains.boundary_note: Engineering/management-oriented (design, compliance, infrastructure). Flags overlap with physical_sciences/earth_atmo, which covers climate and earth-system science; the reclassified GLM lake-calibration task and retired agriculture tasks imply a broader water+environment scope.

subdomains.business_boundary: Data-driven, site-specific crop management services that use geospatial data, sensors, remote sensing, and crop/soil models to optimize planting, nutrient, and input decisions per sub-field zone.
subdomains.occupations: precision agriculture specialist/agronomist; crop consultant; soil scientist; GIS/remote-sensing analyst; agricultural data analyst; VRT equipment technician
subdomains.boundary_note: uncovered_official: true - zero active official ALE tasks; sourced from industry material only. Overlaps env_water (water/nutrient management), visual_media (drone/satellite imagery), and agriculture_env broadly.

candidates.workflow_title: Urban Stormwater Drainage Network Modeling and Green-Infrastructure (LID) Design
candidates.workflow_summary: Build and calibrate a rainfall-runoff model of an urban drainage network, then size and evaluate gray and green-infrastructure (LID) controls so runoff volume and pollutant loads meet a regulatory target.
candidates.source_reference: https://www.epa.gov/water-research/storm-water-management-model-swmm (EPA SWMM page, fetched and read this round)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Subcatchment GIS layers (imperviousness, slope, land use), pipe/network geometry and node data, rainfall time series, target design storm and local stormwater regulations, monitored flow/quality data for calibration.
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert must supply or be authorized to use real municipality/consultant project data or a de-identified synthetic equivalent.
candidates.task_input: A drainage network specification plus rainfall and regulatory targets; the model must be built, run, and validated against them.
candidates.professional_operations: Delineate subcatchments, assign hydrologic parameters, build the network, run design-storm and long-term simulations, test LID/BMP controls, and report peak flows and pollutant reductions.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A calibrated SWMM model plus a design report recommending pipe and green-infrastructure sizing with flow and quality results.
candidates.success_criteria: Simulated peak flow and volume match monitored/design values within stated tolerance and selected controls meet the regulatory detention/quality target.
candidates.verification_approach: Run the submitted model headlessly and compare output hydrographs/pollutographs against withheld target observations or design constraints.
candidates.platform_dependencies: SWMM is open-source and cross-platform (C engine); runnable via Python pyswmm or CLI on Linux; no GPU needed.
candidates.blocking_risks: Requires a valid network dataset; proprietary commercial software or licensed rainfall data could block Linux automation.
candidates.expert_capability: Hydrology and open-channel hydraulics, stormwater regulations, and SWMM modeling/calibration.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps env_water flood/hydraulics candidates and, for water quality, physical_sciences/earth_atmo watershed science.
candidates.granularity_check: End-to-end (build, calibrate, design, report); not a single operation.

candidates.workflow_title: Groundwater Flow Model Development and Aquifer Calibration
candidates.workflow_summary: Assemble a conceptual hydrostratigraphic model, build a MODFLOW numerical model, calibrate hydraulic parameters against observed heads, and report water budget, heads, and drawdown.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Geologic logs and aquifer-layer geometry, well locations and pumping rates, observed head data, recharge and boundary conditions, hydraulic conductivity estimates.
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert must provide field/well data or a de-identified synthetic aquifer dataset with permission to use.
candidates.task_input: Aquifer geometry, boundary conditions, pumping, and observed heads; produce a calibrated model and water budget.
candidates.professional_operations: Define grid and layers, assign parameters, run steady/transient simulations, calibrate to observed heads, and evaluate the water budget and capture zones.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A calibrated MODFLOW model with a technical memo on heads, water budget, and recharge/discharge.
candidates.success_criteria: Calibrated heads match observations within accepted residual targets and the water balance is closed.
candidates.verification_approach: Run the model headlessly (FloPy/MODFLOW 6) and check head residuals and water-balance error against thresholds.
candidates.platform_dependencies: MODFLOW 6 and FloPy are open-source and run on Linux; no GPU.
candidates.blocking_risks: Large/complex datasets and proprietary GUI tools (Visual MODFLOW/GMS) may be needed; conceptual-model judgment is hard to automate.
candidates.expert_capability: Hydrogeology, groundwater hydraulics, and MODFLOW/FloPy calibration.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps physical_sciences/earth_atmo for subsurface/earth-science groundwater studies.

candidates.workflow_title: Riverine Hydrologic-Hydraulic Modeling and Floodplain Delineation
candidates.workflow_summary: Develop a watershed hydrologic model to derive design flows and a hydraulic model to compute water-surface profiles, then delineate floodplain boundaries and flood risk.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: DEM/terrain and channel cross-sections, stream geometry, Manning roughness, land use, precipitation/flow data, and design storm or return-period flow.
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert supplies terrain and hydrologic data or an authorized de-identified study dataset.
candidates.task_input: Terrain, channel geometry, roughness, and rainfall/flow inputs; compute profiles and floodplain maps.
candidates.professional_operations: Build a HEC-HMS rainfall-runoff model, build HEC-RAS geometry, run steady/unsteady flows, and map water-surface elevations onto terrain.
candidates.expected_deliverable: Water-surface profiles, flood depth/extent map, and a flood-risk summary.
candidates.success_criteria: Modeled stages/flows reproduce observed or expected values and floodplain extents are hydraulically consistent with the terrain.
candidates.verification_approach: Run models headlessly (HEC-RAS CLI) and compare computed stages/extents against target values or terrain-derived checks.
candidates.platform_dependencies: HEC-RAS/HEC-HMS official tools are Windows-centric; open-source Linux alternatives exist but may not reproduce official results.
candidates.blocking_risks: Windows-only official tools are a major Linux automation risk; licensed terrain/hydrology data may also block.
candidates.expert_capability: Hydrologic and open-channel hydraulic modeling, FEMA floodplain standards.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps the env_water stormwater candidate and physical_sciences/earth_atmo for rainfall/climate inputs.
candidates.pending_confirmation: Official HEC tools are Windows-only; confirm acceptable Linux equivalents.

candidates.workflow_title: Water Distribution Network Hydraulic Modeling and Calibration
candidates.occupation_scope: Water utility engineer / distribution system modeler
candidates.workflow_summary: Build and calibrate a pressurized pipe network model to evaluate pressures, flows, tank levels, and water age, then recommend operational or capital improvements.
candidates.source_reference: https://www.epa.gov/water-research/epanet (EPA EPANET page, fetched and read this round)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Pipe network geometry, node elevations and demands, pump/valve/tank characteristics, and pressure/flow telemetry for calibration.
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert must supply utility network data or an authorized synthetic benchmark network.
candidates.task_input: Network topology, demands, controls, and observed pressures; produce a calibrated model and analysis.
candidates.professional_operations: Build the network, assign demands and controls, run extended-period simulation, calibrate to telemetry, and analyze fire flow, water age, and energy.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A calibrated EPANET model plus a report on pressures, fire flow, water age, and improvement options.
candidates.success_criteria: Simulated pressures/flows match observed telemetry within tolerance and fire-flow/age criteria are met.
candidates.verification_approach: Run the model via the EPANET toolkit (Python epyt/wntr) and compare node pressures and tank levels to withheld targets.
candidates.platform_dependencies: EPANET is public-domain; the engine and Python toolkits (Wntr/epyt) run on Linux; the official GUI is Windows-only.
candidates.blocking_risks: Utility data may be proprietary; official GUI is Windows-only but headless toolkits mitigate this.
candidates.expert_capability: Pressurized-pipe hydraulics, water utility operations, EPANET calibration.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Minimal; touches municipal/civil infrastructure rather than other research subdomains.

candidates.workflow_title: Yield Monitor Data Cleaning and Yield Map Production
candidates.workflow_summary: Clean combine yield-monitor data (remove header turns, speed/moisture/overlap errors), georeference to the field, and produce a calibrated yield map with field-level statistics.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Raw yield-monitor point/log data with GPS, harvest moisture, field boundary polygon, and calibration/ground-truth yield (scale tickets).
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert provides real or de-identified farm yield data with farmer permission.
candidates.task_input: Raw yield log plus field boundary; produce a cleaned, calibrated yield map.
candidates.professional_operations: Filter outliers and non-crop passes, correct moisture and speed, interpolate to a raster, normalize to field average, and compute zone statistics.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A calibrated yield raster/map plus summary statistics and an error report.
candidates.success_criteria: Map total reconciles with scale-ticket weight within tolerance and spatial patterns match agronomic expectations.
candidates.verification_approach: Automate cleaning and compare computed field total/mean to withheld scale-ticket targets.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Open-source Python/GDAL/R on Linux; no GPU; commercial software (SMS, AgLeader) optional.
candidates.blocking_risks: Raw log formats are proprietary and varied; cleaning rules are partly expert judgment.
candidates.expert_capability: Yield monitor data formats, geostatistics/interpolation, agronomic QA.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps visual_media/geospatial (raster mapping) and agriculture_env field data.
candidates.granularity_check: End-to-end from raw log to calibrated map, not a single filter.

candidates.workflow_title: Management Zone Delineation from Soil, Yield, and Remote-Sensing Layers
candidates.workflow_summary: Fuse multi-year yield, soil sampling, electrical conductivity, and NDVI imagery to delineate stable sub-field management zones for targeted management.
candidates.source_reference: https://www.mdpi.com/3043-1204/1/1/3 (MDPI management-zone delineation) and http://www.omafra.gov.on.ca/english/crops/pub811/pub811.pdf (OMAFRA soil sampling)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Multi-year yield maps, grid/zone soil sample lab results, soil EC/topography data, and satellite/drone NDVI rasters.
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert supplies farm spatial layers and soil lab data with permission or a de-identified dataset.
candidates.task_input: Stacked geospatial layers; produce a defensible management-zone map.
candidates.professional_operations: Normalize and co-register layers, apply clustering (k-means/fuzzy) or weighted overlay, validate zones against yield/soil, and assign zone attributes.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A zone map with per-zone soil and yield characterization and delineation rationale.
candidates.success_criteria: Zones are spatially coherent, discriminate yield/soil properties, and reproduce expert-defined reference zones.
candidates.verification_approach: Compare algorithmic zones to withheld expert/reference zones and check within- vs between-zone variance.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Python/R GIS (scikit-learn, rasterio) on Linux; no GPU; commercial zone tools optional.
candidates.blocking_risks: Zone correctness is partly subjective; requires clean co-registered multi-year data.
candidates.expert_capability: Soil science, spatial statistics/clustering, agronomic interpretation.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps visual_media (imagery) and env_water for drainage/soil-water interactions.

candidates.workflow_title: Variable-Rate Application Prescription Map Development and Execution
candidates.workflow_summary: Convert field data into a spatially explicit variable-rate prescription (seed, fertilizer, or lime) and translate it to controller-ready format for application.
candidates.source_reference: https://www.extension.purdue.edu/extmedia/AE/SSM-2-W.pdf (Purdue Map- Versus Sensor-Based Variable Rate Application)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Yield/soil/zone layers, crop and input economic parameters, equipment controller format specs, and rate-response agronomy rules.
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert provides field layers and agronomic rate rules with farmer/company permission.
candidates.task_input: Zone/soil/yield data plus agronomic rate rules; produce a controller-ready prescription.
candidates.professional_operations: Set rate equations or thresholds per zone, smooth/classify rates, export to ISO/controller format, and verify controller compatibility.
candidates.expected_deliverable: A prescription map (rate by zone) plus a verification report of total input vs. plan.
candidates.success_criteria: Prescription rates follow agronomic rules, total applied matches plan within tolerance, and the file loads correctly in the target controller.
candidates.verification_approach: Validate rate logic against the supplied rule set and check the output file against controller schema/unit constraints.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Python/GDAL on Linux for map generation; controller compatibility may require proprietary desktop software or a physical display.
candidates.blocking_risks: Proprietary controller formats and machine-specific as-applied verification are hard to test in pure Linux.
candidates.expert_capability: Agronomy (rate-response), VRT controller formats, spatial data handling.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps precision_ag management-zone and yield candidates and env_water nutrient management.
candidates.granularity_check: End-to-end (data to controller-ready file), not just a rate formula.

candidates.workflow_title: Crop Model Calibration and Scenario Simulation for Yield and Nitrogen
candidates.workflow_summary: Calibrate a process-based crop model (APSIM/DSSAT) to local trials, then simulate management and climate scenarios to optimize yield and nitrogen use.
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Field trial observations (phenology, biomass, yield, soil moisture/N), daily weather, soil profile data, cultivar parameters, and management schedules.
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert supplies trial and weather data or an authorized public experimental dataset.
candidates.task_input: Weather, soil, management, and observed crop data; produce a calibrated model and scenario results.
candidates.professional_operations: Set up model files, calibrate cultivar/soil parameters to observations, validate on held-out data, and run scenario ensembles.
candidates.expected_deliverable: Calibrated model files plus scenario comparison (yield, N use efficiency, leaching) and parameter uncertainty.
candidates.success_criteria: Simulated yield/phenology match observations within accepted RMSE/bias and scenarios are internally consistent.
candidates.verification_approach: Run APSIM/DSSAT headlessly and compare simulated vs. withheld observed yield/biomass metrics.
candidates.platform_dependencies: APSIM/DSSAT run on Linux (some components Windows); no GPU.
candidates.blocking_risks: APSIM requires license/registration; DSSAT is Windows-centric but has a CLI; model setup is expert-heavy.
candidates.expert_capability: Crop/soil process modeling, calibration methods, APSIM/DSSAT proficiency.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps physical_sciences/earth_atmo (climate inputs) and env_water (soil water/N leaching).
candidates.pending_confirmation: Confirm APSIM licensing terms for redistribution.

candidates.workflow_title: Satellite/Derived NDVI Crop Health Monitoring and Scouting Support
candidates.workflow_summary: Compute time-series NDVI from satellite or drone imagery over field boundaries, detect anomalies, and produce scouting/action maps for crop health.
candidates.source_reference: https://pubs.ext.vt.edu/BSE/bse-371/bse-371.html (Virginia Tech NDVI Agroclimate App, fetched and read this round)
candidates.expert_raw_materials: Field boundaries, satellite (Sentinel/Landsat) or drone imagery, and ground-truth scouting observations for validation.
candidates.usage_permissions: Expert supplies field boundaries and imagery with license terms (or points to public satellite archives).
candidates.task_input: Field polygons and imagery; produce NDVI time series and anomaly/action maps.
candidates.professional_operations: Clip imagery to fields, compute NDVI, build time series, detect deviations from field mean or phenology, and flag zones for scouting.
candidates.expected_deliverable: NDVI maps/time series plus a prioritized scouting list with confidence.
candidates.success_criteria: Detected anomalies match ground-truth scouting (stress, weeds, disease) with acceptable precision/recall.
candidates.verification_approach: Compare automated anomaly detections against withheld ground-truth scouting labels.
candidates.platform_dependencies: Python (rasterio, Google Earth Engine) on Linux; no GPU; cloud imagery requires API keys/network.
candidates.blocking_risks: Cloud API credentials and imagery licensing; drone imagery processing can need proprietary tools.
candidates.expert_capability: Remote sensing, vegetation indices, crop phenology/stress interpretation.
candidates.cross_domain_overlap: Overlaps visual_media (imagery analysis) and physical_sciences/earth_atmo (remote sensing).
